Subject: MAP: Performance benchmarking & HW sizing — Acme Corp

Olivia — following up from last week’s call with a concrete MAP and benchmarking plan so we can converge on sizing and close timeline. High level: we’ll run a controlled perf sweep across A100, H100, and L40S, evaluating both full-GPU and MIG partitions. Goal metrics: 95th-percentile latency, median latency, TTFT (time-to-first-token), sustained throughput (tokens/sec), and concurrency envelope.

Proposed test matrix (short):
- Models: customer-canned gen model + 4 prompt classes (short/medium/long/history-heavy)
- GPU matrix: A100 (40GB), H100 (Hopper 80GB), L40S (48GB); MIG configs: 1g.5gb+ variants where available
- Concurrency: 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 (target steady-state and spike)
- Metrics: P50/P95 latency, TTFT, tokens/sec, 99% CPU/GPU utilization thresholds, memory headroom
- Environment: Redwood private sandbox (us-west-2) with identical NVMe-backed checkpoint store

Deliverables and timeline (MAP milestones):
1) Test harness + dataset handshake — Aug 4
2) Run baseline sweeps (A100/H100/L40S) — Aug 5–8
3) Deep MIG experiments + stability tests — Aug 9–10
4) Consolidated sizing recommendation + MAP update — Aug 11
5) Executive review + signoff / proposed close — Aug 12

Can you confirm the dataset sample and whether we should include a production-like prefix cache scenario? Also confirm if Acme needs throughput prioritization (cost-sensitive) or latency-first sizing. I’ve attached a short template and a proposed MAP PDF to make signoff straightforward.

Thanks,
Jordan

Thanks — good questions. TL;DR: we’ll report both host-side TTFT and wire-RTT-included TTFT. Our primary SLA artifact will surface the network-inclusive TTFT (that’s what we’ll map to P50/P95). Details below:

Definitions:
- TTFT (host only): time from request arrival at Redwood runtime to first token emitted by model process
- TTFT (incl network): measured from when the client request hits the ingress LB to the first byte on the client socket (we’ll capture with distributed tracing)

Looping in a few quick notes from infra:
- MIG: on H100 we see nice isolation at low-concurrency (1–4) but at 8+ the per-partition headroom drops significantly; memory fragmentation and PCIe contention can surprise results
- L40S: excellent cost profile for medium-latency workloads, but TTFT at small batch sizes is usually ~8–12ms slower vs H100 for the same model when kernels are not fused
- A100 (40GB): predictable for large-context runs and better when you need full 40GB for KV cache; A100 80GB would change the calculus but assuming 40 here

I’ll attach a short internal cheat sheet of observed tail behaviors; happy to run a joint test if you want us to spin an H100 node.

Team — attached are the consolidated run results from our sandbox sweep (A100/H100/L40S; MIG runs included). Key takeaways:

- H100 (full GPU) — best median latency and TTFT for short prompts; P95 latency ~12ms better than A100 on the short-prompt class at concurrency 8. Throughput per GPU ~+18% vs A100 under steady-state 16-concurrency.
- A100 (40GB) — wins on large-context stability and when KV cache retention is required (fewer OOMs on large-history workloads).
- L40S — strong cost-performance for throughput-heavy batch jobs; for customer-facing low-latency endpoints it trails H100 by ~83ms P95 depending on kernel/fusion.
- MIG — viable for low-concurrency (<4) but contention shows at 8+; recommend mixed fleet: full GPUs for production endpoints and MIG for dev/batch.

Sizing recommendation (starting point for Acme):
- Customer-facing low-latency endpoints: H100 full-GPU fleet, 3 nodes (2 active + 1 buffer) for initial 200 qps SLA (based on observed tokens/sec)
- Batch/analytics jobs: L40S clusters using 1:3 density; autoscale to handle peak windows
- KV cache heavy routes: reserve A100 capacity for large-history features (pin versions)

Attachments: consolidated CSV (perf_results_08010.csv), raw logs tar (lab_logs_08009.tar.gz) and our recommended MAP draft. I flagged the parts of the MAP that require Acme signoff (budget for H100 reserved capacity / decision on cache-first vs latency-first).
